links.note: British tariffs on cotton imports causing Indian textile exports to fall is the trade-in-goods flow being shaped by policy, the first of 23877's three flows. This chapter's Indian-trade-and-colonialism section has no concept of its own (23879 covers only Indian traders and indentured labour), so 23877 is the nearest. The sharper home for this stem is 23892 in chapter 23708, if it is ever re-chaptered.

Henry Ford adapting the assembly line for cars belongs to the inter-war economy that 23880 heads. FRAME GAP: the rise of mass production and consumption has no concept here; 23881 is specifically the post-1929 Depression, which this predates and fed.

The Irish potato famine of 1845-49 is the travelling-foods passage - Ireland's poorest peasants became so dependent on the potato that disease in the crop brought mass starvation. 23869. DEFECT: the stem's figure reads 10,000,000; the text says about a million.

Poverty, hunger, crowded cities and deadly diseases driving Europeans to flee for America closes the conquest-disease-and-trade section, immediately before the plantations growing cotton and sugar for European markets - 23876. 23875 is disease among native Americans as a weapon of conquest, not disease in Europe as a push factor.
